description: Roughly 3,690 Nigerians in the United States face deportation, drawn from ICE data showing 1,445,549 non-citizens on the non-detained docket with final removal orders as of 24 November 2024.
energy_note: Three thousand six hundred and ninety names on a list.

aspect: EXAMPLE - removed to Ghana, then bussed
description: In September 2025 Ghana's president said a group of 14 deportees including Nigerians and one Gambian had arrived in Ghana, with the government facilitating the Nigerians' onward return home by bus - part of an arrangement under which Ghana accepts third-country nationals removed from the US, limited to West African nationals.
energy_note: Deported to a country you are not from, then put on a coach.

aspect: The removal severs everything at once
description: Employment, tenancy, bank accounts, a course mid-way, and frequently children who remain. There is no wind-down period and no mechanism to return for one.
energy_note: A life ended by an itinerary.

description: Removal typically carries a multi-year or permanent bar on return, so a family split by a deportation is split for the length of the bar rather than the length of the flight.
energy_note: Ten years, before you may even apply again.
